experiment: E5 DROPWATCH-S: does STANCE-ESCALATION rescue the closed-loop repair controller on an aggressive compressor (gpt-5.5), where the original pin-based DROPWATCH failed (gate FAIL, dropwatch_esc-pin_fair +0.000)?
basis: Rescue diagnostic (commit 11cc9d3) proved the pin_oracle re-injection CEILING on gpt-5.5 lifts from ~0.04 (neutral compression) to 0.52 [.32,.72] under a FAITHFUL compression stance; salience content-labeling did NOT help (0.04). So the rescue lever is the compressor's STANCE, not which facts are pinned. E5 builds that lever into the detect+repair loop and tests it end-to-end with a gate.
model: openai/gpt-5.5 (hardest failing model; reasoning_effort='none' + temp=0). Regime identical to E4: M=24 mixed, K=16, budget=25, B_ri=4, theta=0.35, n=100. strict-min estimand, paired-over-facts bootstrap.

policies.pin_fair: fixed random B_ri re-inject, neutral compression [original E4 gate baseline]
policies.dropwatch_esc: adaptive+escalate re-inject, neutral compression [original method; FAILED on gpt-5.5]
policies.faithful_always: no re-inject, faithful compression EVERY hop [pure Moat-2 baseline: 'just always preserve']
policies.pin_fair_faithful: fixed random re-inject + faithful compression every hop [isolates adaptivity given stance]
policies.dropwatch_stance: adaptive+escalate re-inject + faithful compression on repairing hops, neutral when quiescent [THE METHOD]

PRE_REGISTERED_COMPARISONS.PRIMARY_rescue_gate: dropwatch_stance strict-min minus pin_fair strict-min: paired bootstrap CI lower bound > 0 AND dropwatch_stance cost_per_hop <= pin_fair (4.0). PASS -> stance-escalation rescues the method where pinning could not, on the hardest aggressive compressor. FAIL -> report honestly.
PRE_REGISTERED_COMPARISONS.stance_lever: dropwatch_stance minus dropwatch_esc, CI-excl-0 -> the stance lever adds value to the SAME re-injection logic (isolates stance from targeting).
PRE_REGISTERED_COMPARISONS.adaptivity_control: dropwatch_stance minus faithful_always. If ~0 (CI includes 0) -> the adaptive detector does NOT earn its keep on aggressive compressors and the honest recommendation is 'just always use preservation stance'; report that. If > 0 -> targeted re-injection adds value on top of stance.

predictions.primary: dropwatch_stance beats pin_fair (rescue gate PASS); point ~ +0.15..0.40, cost < 4.0 (adaptive, faithful adds no API calls).
predictions.stance_lever: dropwatch_stance > dropwatch_esc, CI-excl-0 (the whole point of the diagnostic).
predictions.adaptivity: GENUINELY UNCERTAIN and the most interesting control. faithful_always may capture most of the gain (stance does the heavy lifting per the diagnostic); if so, dropwatch_stance - faithful_always ~ small/zero and the honest headline becomes 'on aggressive compressors, preservation stance is the fix; adaptive detection is optional'. I will report whichever way it lands and NOT bury a null adaptivity result.
predictions.pin_fair_faithful: expected close to faithful_always (fixed pinning under neutral was already ~useless; adding stance mainly helps via the stance).

honest_notes: New cache data/cache_e5_gpt-5.5.json -> no collision with e4/rescue caches.

Reproducibility caveat (from the diagnostic): gpt-5.5 temp=0 API is not fully deterministic; 16-hop chains amplify token diffs. Within-run 6-policy comparison shares the noise and is valid; absolute levels carry run-to-run wobble. The gate is a within-run contrast.
cost metric = re-injection slots/hop (faithful stance adds no API call). faithful compression may emit longer carries; that is a token consideration, not counted here, noted for honesty.

If gate PASSES on gpt-5.5, the method (DROPWATCH-S) is the rescue; Sonnet/mini confirmation can follow. If adaptivity control is null, the deliverable is still a method (stance-escalation) plus an honest 'detector-optional' scope.
